title: the log wrapper cannot be declined project-side: every value of log: wraps, and the - sentinel is scoped to the catalogue's value (from Intent 0391)
body:
Moved from Intent issue 0391 by intent-vc at 2026-09-14 17:47Z: the fix's home is devbin's own lib/resolve, since Intent's bin/.devbin/ is a checksummed vendored copy that devbin upgrade overwrites (Laksa's vendored one-line fix was already overwritten that way).


devbin's log wrapper cannot be declined project-side. dc's four-value sweep in Laksa (2026-09-12, recorded in Laksa's `intent/whiteboard/vc/.history/20260914/inbox.dc-premigration.md`): `log:` absent inherits the catalogue row and wraps; `log: false` is the non-empty string `false` and wraps; `log: ""` is empty, so the catalogue fallback reinstates the suffix and wraps (the fallback is deliberate: a project overriding a gate's `run:` without declaring `log:` would otherwise silently stop sealing); `log: "-"` is non-empty, so it skips the fallback and wraps anyway with the suffix `-`, because the `[ "$log_suffix" = "-" ]` mapping sits inside the fallback branch and applies only to what `builtin_option_suffix` returns, the catalogue's value and never the project's.

Fix, vendored in Laksa's `lib/resolve` as one line: honour an explicit project-side `-` BEFORE the fallback. The fallback protects a project that forgot to declare `log:`; an explicit sentinel is not forgetting. Upstream home: `bin/.devbin/lib/resolve`. Laksa's config.yaml carries the sweep inline as the record. Lane: dc.




## Closed 2026-09-14 -- fixed in devbin's own resolver, reviewed, and every arm watched red and then mutated

**The fix.** `gate_log_suffix` in `lib/runlog` is the one function that says what a declared `log:` means, and it now prints nothing for a decline: `-`, `false`, `no` or `0`. `run_option` and `run_command` in `lib/resolve` resolve the declared value through it ONCE, before the test that decides whether to seal, and hand that resolved value to the seal. They used to test the raw value, so any non-empty value sealed. The `-` mapping that sat inside the catalogue fallback is removed rather than kept alongside, so the sentinel means the same thing from either source and at either level.

**What deliberately did not change.** An EMPTY `log:` still falls back to the catalogue row, as this issue says it must: an override that says nothing about sealing does not stop sealing.

**`false`, `no` and `0` decline as well as `-`, approved by hv on 2026-09-14.** They are the spellings devbin already reads as false for `enabled:`, and `true`, `yes` and `1` already meant "seal it, named after the option". Laksa's vendored one-line fix honoured `-` alone.

**The first cut was incomplete, and a review caught it before it landed.** A critic-shell review of the uncommitted diff found `run_command` still resolving `log:` a second time when naming the seal: harmless for every name in use, and a refusal for a command named `0`, whose resolved suffix `0` is itself a decline. Both paths now pass the suffix as resolved. A resolution that FAILS is refused rather than run unsealed -- `run_option` reports and returns, because `run_all` calls it in a loop, and `run_command` dies. That failure branch has no arm, and says so here: the resolver can only fail if `tr` does, and a broken `tr` breaks the dispatcher long before it.

**The same review found a pre-existing assertion that could never fail, in the test these arms extend.** "a config run: override of a catalogue gate keeps its seal and its grammar" ended `refute_file_contains ... "^$"`, which grep -F reads as the literal characters `^$`. So the "and its grammar" half had never been tested. It now asserts the seal holds `** TEST FAILED **` and does NOT hold the log-tail fallback -- under the generic default that line matches nothing and the seal becomes the fallback, so the pair is what tells the inherited xcodebuild grammar from the default one.

**Arms, in `tests/unit/builtins.bats`, each run against the unfixed code first:**

- a project-side `log: "-"` declines the seal a catalogue gate would otherwise inherit -- red before the fix, with the seal written as `<stamp>.-.out`
- `log: false`, `no` and `0` decline exactly as `-` does, each held to everything the `-` arm asserts -- red before the fix, with a `tmp/` seal under `false`
- a command-level `log: "-"` runs the command bare -- red before the fix, with `tmp/greet/<stamp>.-.out`
- the control: an EMPTY `log:` still inherits the catalogue's seal -- green before and after, as it has to be
- added after the review: a command-level `log: true` seals under the command's own name, because no fixture had sent one through `run_command`'s resolver

**Mutations, each confirmed applied before its run and restored and verified by `cmp` after:**

- deleting the decline arm turned the three decline arms red and left the control and the `log: true` arm green
- dropping only `false` turned exactly the `false, no and 0` arm red
- making the catalogue fallback never run turned the control red, with the existing seal-and-grammar test -- so the control is one that can fail
- stopping an override inheriting the catalogue GRAMMAR turned exactly the repaired seal-and-grammar test red
- sealing `log: true` under the literal word rather than the name turned exactly the command-level `log: true` arm red
- making the bare path skip the tool turned the `-` and the `false, no and 0` arms red, which is the regression "exactly as - does" now guards

Documented in `docs/configuration.md` and in the vendored `lib/config.reference.yaml`.

**Filed rather than widened:** the review also found the true and false words, and the `-` sentinel, written out at thirteen sites with nothing holding them in step. That is 0066.

**The full suite**, on a clone carrying exactly this change together with the 0056 census column and the doctor half of 0062, and nothing else: 1073 of 1073, rc 0 captured directly after bats, three skips each stating its own reason, no stray output.

**It reaches the fleet at the next re-vendor, not before.** Laksa's hand fix was overwritten by `upgrade`, which is why this issue moved here; until a sweep delivers this resolver, every estate still runs the old one.
